viralWarning: Antibiotics are not effective for viral infections like flu or most colds. Rest, fluids, and medical advice when needed matter most.
bacterialNote: Some bacterial infections may need antibiotics—only a clinician can decide. Never use leftover antibiotics.
infoCardBody: Misuse drives resistance. Kurdana Health encourages informed conversations with licensed professionals.
dailyTip1: Drink water first thing; mild dehydration mimics fatigue.
dailyTip2: A 10-minute walk after meals supports steady energy.
dailyTip3: Keep a consistent sleep window—even on weekends.
dailyTip4: Pair protein with fiber at lunch to avoid afternoon crashes.
dailyTip5: Step outside for natural light early; it anchors your rhythm.
miniWrong: Not quite—antibiotics target bacteria, not viruses.
miniRight: Correct. Using antibiotics only when appropriate protects everyone.
skinRoutine_oily:
Morning: gentle gel cleanser, niacinamide serum (if tolerated), oil-free moisturizer, SPF 30+.
Evening: double cleanse on sunscreen days, same moisturizer, optional light retinoid 2×/week if your clinician agrees.
skinRoutine_dry:
Morning: cream cleanser, hydrating serum (hyaluronic acid), rich moisturizer, SPF.
Evening: cleanse gently, layer moisturizer; consider occlusive balm on very dry zones.
skinRoutine_combo:
Morning: mild cleanser, lightweight gel on T-zone, richer cream on cheeks, SPF.
Evening: balance zones—don’t over-strip oily areas.
skinRoutine_sensitive:
Morning: fragrance-free cleanser, soothing moisturizer, mineral SPF.
Evening: one new product at a time; patch test; prioritize barrier repair.
skinTips_oily: Avoid overwashing (it can trigger more oil). Blot, don’t rub. Non-comedogenic labels help.
skinTips_dry: Short, lukewarm showers. Apply moisturizer to slightly damp skin. Humidify if air is dry.
skinTips_combo: Zone care beats one-size-fits-all. Exfoliate gently and sparingly.
skinTips_sensitive: Fewer ingredients, slower introductions, and sunscreen daily—barrier first.
